title: Derived module tensor exchange over a flat algebra
statement:
Let $R\to S$ be a flat homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], let $K^\bullet$ be any cochain complex of $S$-modules, and let $N$ be an $R$-module. Use ordinary tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], derived categories with localization functors $Q_R,Q_S$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and total tensor with differential $d(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^{\deg x}x\otimes dy$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Let $F^\bullet\to N[0]$ be any free $R$-module resolution [def-weil-pbc-free-module], with $F^i=0$ for $i>0$. Derived tensor is computed on K-flat resolutions [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. There is a canonical isomorphism in $D(S)$
$$Q_S\operatorname{Tot}(K^\bullet\otimes_R F^\bullet)\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ Q_S(K^\bullet)\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}(S\otimes_R N)[0],$$
where the left side has its $S$-action on $K^\bullet$. On forgetting to $D(R)$ its source represents $\operatorname{Res}_{R\to S}Q_S(K^\bullet)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N[0]$. The isomorphism is natural in $K^\bullet$, in $N$, and in maps between augmented free resolutions. Its composite with the canonical derived-to-ordinary map and the ordinary balancing isomorphism
$$Q_S(K^\bullet)\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}(S\otimes_R N)[0]\longrightarrow Q_S\operatorname{Tot}(K^\bullet\otimes_S(S\otimes_R N)[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_S\operatorname{Tot}(K^\bullet\otimes_R N[0])$$
is the localization of the augmentation $1_K\otimes(F^\bullet\to N[0])$. No boundedness of $K^\bullet$, Noetherian hypothesis or finite-generation hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Put $G=S\otimes_R F$ and $M=(S\otimes_R N)[0]$, with augmentation $e=1_S\otimes\epsilon:G\to M$. Flat tensor exactness [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] applied to the augmented resolution shows that $e$ is a quasi-isomorphism. A basis $(f_i)$ of $F^q$ gives the basis $(1\otimes f_i)$ of $G^q$: the inverse coordinate maps send $s\otimes\sum r_if_i$ to the finitely supported family $(sr_i)$. Free modules are flat directly: tensoring with a free module is a direct sum of copies, and a direct sum of injective maps is injective by its finite-support coordinates. Thus both $F$ over $R$ and $G$ over $S$ are bounded-above complexes of flat modules, hence K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat]. Neither assertion involves $K$.

source.place: Tags 0661 (lemma-base-change-comparison), free-resolution argument; 064K (lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism); flat exactness Tag 00HD

proof.text: In every bidegree define $b:K\otimes_R F\to K\otimes_S G$ by $x\otimes f\mapsto x\otimes(1\otimes f)$. Its inverse is $x\otimes(s\otimes f)\mapsto sx\otimes f$. The tensor relations make both maps well-defined and $S$-linear, and their composites are the identity on pure tensors. They preserve bidegrees and commute with both differentials, since $d_K(sx)=s\,d_Kx$ and $d_G(s\otimes f)=s\otimes d_Ff$. Hence they commute with $d_K\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_F$ on bidegree $(p,q)$ and give inverse maps on each direct-sum total degree. This proves a natural chain isomorphism $b:\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes_R F)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes_S G)$, using the same $S$-action on $K$ throughout.

proof.text: Use the one-object site of [lem-trf-one-point-derived-ring-identification] for each coefficient ring. Every presheaf on this site is a sheaf, so sheafification is the additive identity and the sheafification hypotheses hold. Write $\mu_{U,V}:QU\otimes^{\mathbf L}QV\to Q\operatorname{Tot}(U\otimes V)$ for the canonical natural lax tensorator of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor]. Its invertibility when either factor is K-flat applies to $(K,G)$ by step 1. Define the required isomorphism in $D(S)$ by $\alpha=(1\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q_Se)\,\mu_{K,G}^{-1}\,Q_Sb$. All three factors are invertible: $Q_Se$ is invertible by localization and step 1. After forgetting to $R$, the source is literally $Q_R\operatorname{Tot}((\operatorname{Res}K)\otimes_R F)$. The same K-flat comparison over $R$, followed by $Q_R\epsilon$, identifies it with $(\operatorname{Res}Q_SK)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N[0]$. Restriction preserves cohomology because kernels and images of module maps are unchanged on underlying abelian groups, so it induces the asserted functor on derived categories.

proof.text: For a cochain map $a:K\to K_1$ and an augmented resolution map $u:F\to F_1$ over $v:N\to N_1$, balancing gives $b_1(a\otimes u)=(a\otimes(1_S\otimes u))b$, and augmentedness gives $e_1(1_S\otimes u)=(1_S\otimes v)e$. Naturality of $\mu$ therefore gives naturality of $\alpha$ for these maps. Every $v$ admits such a $u$ by [lem-weil-pbc-free-complex-maps-to-resolution], reindexing $F^i$ as $F_{-i}$. Two lifts of $v$ are homotopic by [new-t4-augmented-resolution-lift-homotopy]; its projectivity hypothesis holds since a map out of a free module lifts through a surjection by lifting the images of its basis. Total tensor respects homotopies by [lem-sfb-total-tensor-homotopy], so the resulting maps in $D(S)$ agree. Taking $v=1_N$ in both directions gives mutually inverse canonical comparisons between different free resolutions: their composites lift $1_N$ and hence are homotopic to identities. This proves independence of resolution and naturality in $N$ as well as in all specified augmented resolution maps.

source.place: Tag 00LS (lemma-compare-resolutions), parts (1),(2); total tensor on homotopy classes: more-algebra.tex lemma-derived-tor-homotopy; naturality of the construction in Tag 0661

proof.text: The canonical derived-to-ordinary map in the statement is $\mu_{K,M}$. Its naturality for $e:G\to M$ says $\mu_{K,M}(1\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q_Se)=Q_S(1_K\otimes e)\mu_{K,G}$. Let $c:\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes_S M)\to\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes_R N[0])$ be ordinary balancing, $x\otimes(s\otimes n)\mapsto sx\otimes n$. Substitution of the formula for $\alpha$ cancels $\mu_{K,G}$ and gives $Q_Sc\,\mu_{K,M}\alpha=Q_S(c(1_K\otimes e)b)$. The chain composite on the right takes $x\otimes f$ to $x\otimes\epsilon(f)$, and is therefore exactly the stated tensor augmentation. This calculation uses naturality of the specified tensorator, not an arbitrary isomorphism between its endpoints. Infinite free bases and unbounded $K$ cause no convergence issue: each element of a total degree has finite support in the direct sum.
